units.source_text: （手持单程车票，悲伤的布鲁斯）……想唱歌的话，请随便唱吧。

en.t: (Holding a one-way ticket, a sad blues)... If you want to sing, go ahead and sing as you please.

units.source_text: 实际上，捏着单程车票的人，绝不会唱那种歌。

en.t: In fact, people clutching one-way tickets would never sing that sort of song.

units.source_text: 只捏着单程车票的人们的鞋后跟，光是踏着小石子也已经磨秃。

en.t: The heels of those who clutch only one-way tickets are already worn bald just from stepping on pebbles.
They can no longer take another step forward.

units.source_text: 想唱歌的是有往返车票的“布鲁斯”。

en.t: The one that wants to sing is the blues with a round-trip ticket.

units.source_text: 所谓单程车票，就是昨天和今天、今天和明天都失去联系的凌乱生活。

en.t: A so-called one-way ticket is a disorderly life in which yesterday and today, and today and tomorrow, have lost all connection.

units.source_text: 能够哼着小曲吟唱伤痕累累的单程车票的，肯定是捏着往返车票的人。

en.t: The ones who can hum and sing of a scarred one-way ticket must surely be people clutching round-trip tickets.

units.source_text: 所以，不能把回去的那一半车票弄丢，不能让人给偷走了。

en.t: So you must not lose the return half of the ticket, and you must not let anyone steal it.

units.source_text: 那样急躁，买股票，办生命保险，两面三刀对付工会和上司。

en.t: That is why they grow so anxious, buy stocks, take out life insurance, and play a double game with the union and their bosses.

units.source_text: 单程车票的那帮家伙想不开，大声恶叫，

en.t: The one-way-ticket crowd broods themselves into a corner and howls abuse at the top of their lungs,

units.source_text: 声音从浴室的放水口，厕所的下水道腾起，

en.t: and their voices rise up from the bathroom drain and the toilet sewer,

units.source_text: 人们想堵住耳朵，便故意放大电视机的音量，

en.t: so people, trying to block their ears, deliberately turn up the television volume,

units.source_text: 一个劲儿地哼唱单程车票的布鲁斯。

en.t: and keep on humming the one-way-ticket blues.

units.source_text: 被攫住的人们的歌，哪怕是往返车票的“布鲁斯”也一点不会觉得诧异。

en.t: As songs of people who have been seized, even a round-trip-ticket blues would not seem strange in the least.
